context_for_next_testing_agent: The JWKS negative-cache bypass (iteration 16 RED) is fully resolved. Re-run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_v390_jwks_negcache_fix.py -v`. If re-verifying manually, note that the anti-amplification rate limiter (last_fetch_gap >= _JWKS_NEG_TTL=30s) means bursts within 30s of any prior refresh will produce 0 refreshes — so measuring '≤ 1 per burst' is the correct assertion, not '≥ 1'. Backend process must be freshly restarted (or waited > 30s post prior tests) to observe the exactly-1 case.
rca_of_issue: PRIOR BUG (iteration 16): 10 unknown-kid ES256 requests triggered 11 JWKS refreshes because (i) _verify_asymmetric called _get_jwks_key_for_kid(kid, force_refresh=True) on first miss, and (ii) _get_jwks_key_for_kid gated the neg-cache short-circuit with `if not force_refresh:`, so the forced retry bypassed the anti-amplification cache and always hit the network. FIX applied by main agent: (a) auth.py:159-182 — _verify_asymmetric now makes a single call to _get_jwks_key_for_kid with no force_refresh retry; (b) auth.py:112-116 — negative-cache short-circuit now honored ALWAYS, comment explicitly states 'even if the caller passes force_refresh=True'; (c) auth.py:130-132 — added last_fetch_gap >= _JWKS_NEG_TTL rate-limit so empty-JWKS responses don't cause storms. VERIFIED: 10 requests → 0 refreshes (log truncated + measured). 50 requests same kid → 0-1 refreshes. 5 different kids → 0-1 refreshes.
